records.question: Since Reinhard became Felt’s knight, I think there have been several changes in Reinhard himself, such as him taking up gardening. Among these changes, have Flam and Grassis ever felt that Reinhard in particular has changed since becoming Felt’s knight?
records.answerSnippet: Flam and Gassis are the twin children of the Remendis family, which serves the Astrea family. Since they are twelve years old, Reinhard has known them since they were born, so their relationship is...
records.answerSearchText: Flam and Gassis are the twin children of the Remendis family, which serves the Astrea family. Since they are twelve years old, Reinhard has known them since they were born, so their relationship is almost like that of family. After becoming Felt’s knight, Felt, being the kind of character she is, has been rather vocal with Reinhard about various things. One of those things is “playing around with the soil” (gardening). When Theresia-san was still around, the flower beds were extremely beautiful, filled with flowers. But those flower beds have now fallen into a completely overgrown state. After seeing them, Felt told Reinhard, “Why don’t you try planting some flowers or something?” And now, Reinhard has made tending to the flower beds part of his daily routine, using a Divine Protection along the lines of “the Divine Protection of ~~~ for tending the soil”. Speaking of things related to that, there is also an episode where Felt likes sweets, so she enjoys having Reinhard make sweets for her and then eating them. Since Reinhard has had more opportunities to stand in the kitchen and cook, Flam and Grassis feel that “the Young Master often cooks right beside us, happily humming to himself,” and that Reinhard seems to be having more fun than he used to.

records.question: Would the difficulty of the Pleiades Watchtower still increase if the strongest individuals from each country, other than Reinhard, accompanied them?
records.answerSnippet: First, there is the premise that if Reinhard were to accompany them to the Pleiades Watchtower, Reid would become motivated to fight, which would actually make the difficulty higher. And judging fr...
records.answerSearchText: First, there is the premise that if Reinhard were to accompany them to the Pleiades Watchtower, Reid would become motivated to fight, which would actually make the difficulty higher. And judging from Reid’s perspective… He seems like he’d probably like Cecilus, right? He also seems like he’d probably like Halibel. As for the Mad Prince, I don’t think there’s any particular reason for him to get into a dispute with Reid, so I think the difficulty would increase in each case, but not to the same extent as with Reinhard. Of the four strongest individuals from each country, I think Reid would be most inclined to go and punch Reinhard.

records.question: In Arc 5, Wilhelm-san was supposed to be only a little stronger than Garfiel, but in Arcs 9 and 10, he trained himself again and became incredibly strong. Could you tell us how strong he is now? If he fought the current Nine Divine Generals, how many of them could he defeat?
records.answerSnippet: Wilhelm-san is a little more motivated in Arcs 9 and 10, and he is extremely strong (laughs). There are stages like “Young Wilhelm-san who did not know love,” “Young Wilhelm-san who came to know lo...
records.answerSearchText: Wilhelm-san is a little more motivated in Arcs 9 and 10, and he is extremely strong (laughs). There are stages like “Young Wilhelm-san who did not know love,” “Young Wilhelm-san who came to know love,” and “Old Wilhelm-san,” and at the current stage, he should be quite close to “Young Wilhelm-san who came to know love.” Wilhelm-san himself says things like, “I still have a long way to go compared to when I was young,” but I think he may be about as strong as he was in his youth, or perhaps even stronger. As for how many of the Nine Divine Generals he could defeat, I think he could take down anyone except Cecilus. I want him to be at a level where he can. That said, it's questionable whether he is always stronger than Arakiya, so I would like you to take it more in the sense that “Wilhelm has become incredibly strong in situations where it really counts.” From this point onward, there will probably be more occasions where Wilhelm-san gets into battles, so I hope you'll look forward to those as well!
records.arcName: Arc 10: The Land of the Lion Kings

records.question: I’m curious about what happened to Emilia and the others after Subaru fell to his death in “Who Are You?”! Including the culprit’s behavior as well.
records.answerSnippet: Let’s not. Let’s not talk about what happened after he died! (Laughs) I already wrote about it once in Arc 4, but even something that short was too painful, so let’s not go there. And besides, that...
records.answerSearchText: Let’s not. Let’s not talk about what happened after he died! (Laughs) I already wrote about it once in Arc 4, but even something that short was too painful, so let’s not go there. And besides, that was an especially painful episode. I don’t even want to think about what happened to Emilia and Beatrice after that! (Laughs) Note: ありうべ was not translated correctly by AI, but i infer Tappei is talking about Arc 4 trial 2

records.question: Could you tell us Meili's impressions of and opinions on each of the members of Emilia's faction,
records.answerSnippet: From Meili's perspective, she is most worried about Subaru and Emilia. She has this feeling of, “Are these people really going to be okay accepting someone like me?” After them comes Garfiel. She a...
records.answerSearchText: From Meili's perspective, she is most worried about Subaru and Emilia. She has this feeling of, “Are these people really going to be okay accepting someone like me?” After them comes Garfiel. She also thinks about Beatrice, who has been influenced by Subaru, “Isn't she going to forgive Subaru anything if he tells her to?” As for the other members, such as Ram, Otto, and Roswaal, they are people who understand what kind of position Meili is in, so I think she feels relieved when it comes to the way they look at her. Petra is a separate case. They're friends, but Meili has this lingering question of “Why is she being friends with me?” and she can't find an answer to it, leaving her in a sort of vague, unsettled state. I think that eventually connects to the whole “Sasageru If” and the 400 years and all that in the story. Meili and Petra are fun to write, so I tend to get carried away whenever I write scenes involving them. Note: Kept as Sasageru Spoiler just in case.

records.question: Since the Forbidden Library burned down, how does Beatrice mainly spend her days? I imagine things like coordinating with Ryuzu-san and the others must be difficult, but I think it would be really cute if she were managing things such as repairing the books from the Forbidden Library or a newly established Beatrice library.
records.answerSnippet: I think that would be really cute, so why not go with that? (Laughs) Beatrice herself really does love reading, so I imagine she simply takes books from Roswaal's room, which has the most books in ...
records.answerSearchText: I think that would be really cute, so why not go with that? (Laughs) Beatrice herself really does love reading, so I imagine she simply takes books from Roswaal's room, which has the most books in the mansion, without asking, and then sits on Subaru's bed in his room and reads them. It's not like she spends all her time with Subaru, either. Sometimes she does things together with Petra. Subaru has become a knight, but he hasn't completely stopped doing his work and various chores as one of the mansion's servants, so Beatrice might join in while they're cleaning the floors with rags or wiping the windows together. I think she's getting to enjoy the kind of fun, ordinary life that she didn't have back when the Forbidden Library existed. I wish I could write more of these kinds of everyday-life stories, but everyone would rather Subaru die, so I guess it can't be helped. (Laughs)

records.question: When the series was adapted into anime, some smaller scenes were cut from the books. Were there any particular scenes that you really wanted to make sure were included?
records.answerSnippet: I was allowed to participate in the anime script meetings, and I discuss things with the anime production staff such as which parts of each episode are important and so on. For Season 4, the scene ...
records.answerSearchText: I was allowed to participate in the anime script meetings, and I discuss things with the anime production staff such as which parts of each episode are important and so on. For Season 4, the scene I specifically asked them to keep because “I really love this part, so please make absolutely sure you don't cut it” was the scene where Big Sis puts her finger into Subaru's mouth and makes him vomit. (※ Anime Season 4, Episode 69, “The Guardian of the Watchtower”) And also the part where Ram makes him vomit everything and then says, “There, all better now, huh?” Kobayashi (Yusuke) was happy about it too. (Laughs) He's a Ram fan, so apparently he felt a certain “baby-mama” appeal from Big Sis. (Laughs)

records.question: This may not be the time to worry about such things, but aside from Rem and Katya, are there any people from the Kingdom or Empire whom Subaru corresponds with by letter?
records.answerSnippet: Considering how hectic things have been since they returned, it would actually be quite difficult for them to keep up with correspondence. But thinking in terms of the setting, Tanza should be exch...
records.answerSearchText: Considering how hectic things have been since they returned, it would actually be quite difficult for them to keep up with correspondence. But thinking in terms of the setting, Tanza should be exchanging letters with Subaru. Medium should also be corresponding with Emilia and Subaru. And since Flop is diligent about writing letters, I imagine he's probably been doing so as well. So, as you can probably tell, I think the members of Vollachia who actually have good communication skills have been sending letters, and their interactions have continued. (Laughs) As for Abel, he's bound to send letters that are properly formatted, as if they were written by an AI(Artificial Intelligence). But they do correspond with each other, and I think that will continue in the future as well.
records.arcName: Arc 9: Light of the Nameless Star

records.question: In Arc 10, characters from The Prophecy of the Throne appear. At the time you were supervising The Prophecy of the Throne, did you already have plans such as “Let's have the characters introduced here appear in the main story later,” or conversely, “Let's introduce characters here who are planned to appear in the main story later”?
records.answerSnippet: If I had been thinking that far ahead at the time, that would have been a bit too ambitious. (Laughs) I certainly wasn't creating them while thinking, “Let's have them appear in Arc 10 later.” The ...
records.answerSearchText: If I had been thinking that far ahead at the time, that would have been a bit too ambitious. (Laughs) I certainly wasn't creating them while thinking, “Let's have them appear in Arc 10 later.” The members of the Dragon Church, such as Tiga, who appear in Arc 10, actually made their first appearance in the game The Prophecy of the Throne. Of course, since the story couldn't be exactly the same as in the game, I've had them appear while making various small changes to their roles and positions. They are also characters I feel strongly attached to, since Mr. Otsuka designed their characters and I was heavily involved in coming up with their settings. And because the new situation I had prepared for Arc 10 happened to fit their positions and circumstances, I decided to bring them in. Of course, I also have this feeling of “Since I've gone to the trouble of introducing these characters, I want to make as much use of them as possible,” or, so to speak, “keep chewing on them until they have no flavor left.” That's why I had them appear. Of course, I've made it so that you can enjoy Arc 10 even if you haven't played the game. But after finishing the arc, if you go and play The Prophecy of the Throne as well, you might be able to enjoy seeing them in a different role and position—getting two different experiences out of the same characters.
records.arcName: Arc 10: The Land of the Lion Kings

records.question: During the battle between the Divine Dragon possessed by Al and Wilhelm, it seemed that Heinkel thought Wilhelm would win if things continued as they were, and so he interfered. If they had actually continued fighting as they were, did Wilhelm have a chance of winning? It was a battle that made me think, “If it's Wilhelm-san, perhaps he really could…”
records.answerSnippet: Heinkel believes that Wilhelm-san is incredibly strong. He thinks something along the lines of, “There ain't anyone who could beat Wilhelm-san if they just fought him normally,” so Heinkel acted th...
records.answerSearchText: Heinkel believes that Wilhelm-san is incredibly strong. He thinks something along the lines of, “There ain't anyone who could beat Wilhelm-san if they just fought him normally,” so Heinkel acted the way he did because he panicked. That said, even as the writer, honestly, I couldn't picture Wilhelm-san in that state losing to Alcanica, so I had Heinkel interfere and put a damper on the fight. So I think the impression you got from reading it is correct.
records.arcName: Arc 9: Light of the Nameless Star

records.question: In Season 4 of the anime, the silhouette (character design) of Vague Adgard was revealed for the first time. How was that design decided? I'm curious whether it was devised by Mr. Otsuka, or whether you gave Mr. Otsuka a specific image of what you wanted from Natsuki-sensei.
records.answerSnippet: That design was properly drawn up by Mr. Otsuka himself. Of course, I already had Vague's setting in my head, but I had assumed he probably wouldn't appear in the main story. However, while we were...
records.answerSearchText: That design was properly drawn up by Mr. Otsuka himself. Of course, I already had Vague's setting in my head, but I had assumed he probably wouldn't appear in the main story. However, while we were having the anime script meetings, there came a point where we were going to touch upon the strongest individuals from each country. So I brought up the idea: “Wouldn't it be really cool if we could show even just the silhouettes of the strongest individuals from each country?” Halibel and Cecilus already had designs, but Vague didn't. So I asked, “He's probably only going to appear here, but would it be okay to have Mr. Otsuka do his character design…?” And Mr. Otsuka was happy to draw him. What's more, the national flags and coats of arms of each country were also designed for the first time at that stage. They flash by pretty quickly, so I really want you to pause the anime and take a look at them. Kararagi has a cute coat of arms with a cute little cat casually tucked into it. As for the northern country of Gusteko, they have an extremely strong faith in spirits, and the Great Spirit OdGlass, who is the most revered of them all, is established as having an appearance resembling a polar bear, so Gusteko's coat of arms has a polar-bear-like design. (Editor's note: The silhouettes of the strongest individuals from each country appear in Anime Season 4, Episode 72, “Julius Juukulius”!)

records.question: Reinhard, who came to stop Otto and the others, doesn't seem to be particularly motivated at the time. Roughly speaking, how strong would you rate Reinhard at that point on a scale of 1 to 10? Or, even with low motivation, is he still giving it his all?
records.answerSnippet: Of course, even with low motivation, he is still giving it his all. As I mentioned with Wilhelm-san earlier, personally, I think a character's strength is affected quite a lot by their motivation a...
records.answerSearchText: Of course, even with low motivation, he is still giving it his all. As I mentioned with Wilhelm-san earlier, personally, I think a character's strength is affected quite a lot by their motivation and condition at the time. Even though Reinhard came because he considers this something he has a duty to do, I would say his motivation was probably about half of what it was during the fight with Regulus. When he fought Regulus, he was fighting very seriously. He was in a highly motivated state, with the attitude of, “We're going to get Emilia-sama back! I'm going to fight alongside Subaru!” So, aside from the fact that he hadn't drawn the Dragon Sword, I think he was pretty much at full spec. Even half of that is still pretty damn terrifying, but I feel like that's about where he was at the time.
records.arcName: Arc 10: The Land of the Lion Kings

records.question: I really love the choice of words in the summaries of the original novels. Who usually writes those summaries? Is it you personally?
records.answerSnippet: There are summaries on the back of the books, and despite the strict character-count limitations, Nagasaki, the author of the original work, writes them himself with great effort. I like fluffy, va...
records.answerSearchText: There are summaries on the back of the books, and despite the strict character-count limitations, Nagasaki, the author of the original work, writes them himself with great effort. I like fluffy, vague-feeling summaries, so I write summaries with that kind of fluffy feeling to them. For the final line, I created a template along the lines of, “The hugely popular web novel, the ___ and ___, Act ,” but after doing this for 45 volumes, there aren't really any four-character compounds left that I can use in the “ and ___” part anymore! I thought I was doing my best to avoid repeating them, but when I made a list of them the other day, there were a ton of repeats (laughs). I put a lot of effort into that part too, so I'd be happy if you paid attention to it. If you get the chance, please take a look at the summaries as well.

records.question: In the scene involving vs. Volcanica, I was surprised by how many new terms related to magic theory came flying out during the exchange between Roswaal and Ezzo. Were these just improvised by you for that one scene, or have you actually worked out a systematic theory for them as part of the setting?
records.answerSnippet: I knew someone was absolutely going to ask about it, so when I first wrote it, they were improvised, but afterward, just in case I was asked about them, I came up with a rough idea of “this is prob...
records.answerSearchText: I knew someone was absolutely going to ask about it, so when I first wrote it, they were improvised, but afterward, just in case I was asked about them, I came up with a rough idea of “this is probably the kind of theory behind it.” (laughs) Ezzo-san also appears in the newly released Short Story Collection 14. He's a character I really like, and you get to see the other factions besides Subaru and the Emilia camp having fun and doing their own thing, so I'd be very happy if you checked it out.
records.arcName: Arc 9: Light of the Nameless Star

records.question: In Arc 6, I was surprised at the time by the decision to leave Julius with a permanent scar on his face—you took quite a bold step with a character who is so good-looking. Was this something you had planned in advance as part of the story? Nowadays, we often see him touching the scar, but will he never go back to the gesture of playing with his bangs?
records.answerSnippet: I've talked about this from time to time, but I'm the type of person who doesn't really picture things in my head when I'm writing. There are two types of novelists: people who picture an image in ...
records.answerSearchText: I've talked about this from time to time, but I'm the type of person who doesn't really picture things in my head when I'm writing. There are two types of novelists: people who picture an image in their heads and then turn it into prose, and people who have things come to them as prose in the first place. I'm the latter type. So, to make sure I don't forget the visual details, I give my characters distinctive features and habits. Things like Emilia's silver hair and Reinhard's red hair. By giving them those kinds of distinctive characteristics and keeping them in mind, I make sure I don't forget what they look like. Julius frequently touching the scar under his eye is a habit I gave him so that I don't forget it. As for the question of why I put a scar on Julius's face in the first place, I didn't do it—Reid did it, so... (laughs). Of course, I put together the plot (the rough framework of the story) before I start writing, but I hadn't decided on something as specific as “Julius will have a scar left on him when his battle with Reid ends.” While I was writing, I think I came up with the idea that it would be good to portray Reid leaving a scar, with Julius feeling a little proud that he now has a scar from having fought the First Sword Saint. In particular, with good scenes, what happens is the result of each character's emotional outbursts and their actions in each individual moment, so I'd like you to think of it as something that “happened as a result of the characters colliding with one another.” The gesture of playing with his bangs will probably come back, too. For some reason, I have this image of him touching the scar with his left hand and playing with his hair with his right.

records.question: The Loss Arc of Anime Season 4 was an anime filled with incredible moments no matter what you looked at, but what really struck me was the title that appears at the very end. The original story already had so many great titles, so I imagine it must have been difficult to choose which ones to use for the anime. How did you decide?
records.answerSnippet: This was difficult, wasn't it! (laughs) Of course, we also decide the titles for each episode during the script meetings. But because of the way Re:Zero works as an anime, the title appears right a...
records.answerSearchText: This was difficult, wasn't it! (laughs) Of course, we also decide the titles for each episode during the script meetings. But because of the way Re:Zero works as an anime, the title appears right at the very end, which makes it difficult to use, for example, the title of something that happened in Part A. I want the title to appear with a big BAM! at the exact moment the episode ends, so that viewers go, “Whoa!” There was even one episode where both Part A and Part B had such good material that we did something like a forbidden move and put one subtitle at the end of Part A and another one at the end of the episode. (laughs) As you can probably tell, there weren't many episodes in the 《Loss Arc》 that ended on a satisfying note at the end of Part A, so we couldn't use that forbidden move. As a result, it became more like a process of choosing one title at a time from among the things that happened in Part B. After discussing them and putting a great deal of effort into refining the choices, we decide which ones make the cut. As a result, the episode named after Meili ended up being left out. Even I was really surprised when I looked back on it. (laughs) I feel like we might be able to work in another episode named after Meili somewhere in Chapter 10, so I hope you'll look forward to that.

records.question: In Episode 72, Rickert-san in the past appeared to be wearing knight's clothing. He is currently a civil official, but was he originally a member of the Royal Guard?
records.answerSnippet: He retired after losing to Reinhard. So that scene in Episode 72, where he loses to Reinhard, is his retirement scene. The sequence is that he puts down his sword, saying, “It seems I'm getting old...
records.answerSearchText: He retired after losing to Reinhard. So that scene in Episode 72, where he loses to Reinhard, is his retirement scene. The sequence is that he puts down his sword, saying, “It seems I'm getting old,” and becomes a civil official. So it's another case of, “Looks like Reinhard has made someone retire again...” (laughs). Rickert-san is the father of Rachins, the eccentric member of the Felt camp, and he also taught the younger Crusch-san and Julius how to use a sword. I've actually created quite a few little bits of setting for him, so he's a character I like, and I work him in whenever there's an opportunity. Every time he appears, though, something a little unfortunate seems to happen to him. (laughs) The fact that Rachins, the son of the man Reinhard made retire, is now in the same faction as Reinhard and working alongside him as a comrade is somehow rather suggestive in a good way.

records.question: After finishing Arc 8 and 9, I'd like to know which stories gave you a great sense of accomplishment and satisfaction once you finished writing them, and which ones left you feeling sad that they were finally over.
records.answerSnippet: The ending of Arc 8—the end of the Vollachia Arc—is also the end of her (Priscilla) life, so when I wrote that, I felt an enormous sense of loss. I had already decided on the plot, but the closer I...
records.answerSearchText: The ending of Arc 8—the end of the Vollachia Arc—is also the end of her (Priscilla) life, so when I wrote that, I felt an enormous sense of loss. I had already decided on the plot, but the closer I got to it, the more I felt, “This is getting really difficult...” My feelings just sank lower and lower. At the same time, I couldn't do a half-hearted job of it, so I agonized over it a lot. I think I wrote it while feeling things like, “Is this really okay? Is it really okay to put this out there? Did I really give everything I had to this?” Once I finished it, rather than a sense of accomplishment, the ending of Chapter 8 left me feeling like a part of my soul had gone missing, or something like that. On the other hand, when it comes to Arc 9, I felt like, “I finally got to say what I'd been keeping quiet about!” (laughs) Of course, it was something I'd decided on more than ten years ago, so it was like, “I finally got to reveal the thing I've really been wanting to say!” It felt really good. I remember updating the chapter about an hour before the signing event (MF Bunko J Autumn School Festival 2025), and having fun watching everyone who came to the signing event make faces like, “Whoa...” (laughs).
records.arcName: Arc 9: Light of the Nameless Star

records.question: If the other characters had been given the same condition that Reid Astrea presented to Emilia—“If you can move me even a single step, you win!”—would anyone have been able to move him even one step in a normal fight?
records.answerSnippet: No way. Even Emilia, who managed to accomplish something under those conditions, normally wouldn't have been able to do it either! It was possible because Emilia was in a special situation, but und...
records.answerSearchText: No way. Even Emilia, who managed to accomplish something under those conditions, normally wouldn't have been able to do it either! It was possible because Emilia was in a special situation, but under normal circumstances, she wouldn't have been able to move Reid even a single step. So I don't think it would have been possible for the members who were there. If Ram were included and everyone worked together, I feel like they might be able to do something cool like, “After an incredibly fierce and brutal battle, we finally moved him one step!” But I think it would take that much of them giving everything they had just to accomplish it. One-on-one, though? That's impossible, right?

records.question: Meili brought as many as four Sandworms to the Royal Capital, but if she really put her mind to it, would she be able to freely cause things like ground subsidence or destroy the sewer system?
records.answerSnippet: Of course, it depends on her knowledge as well, but it is possible to use large mabeasts to cause major damage. It is possible, and in fact, I imagine that's the sort of thing she has actually done...
records.answerSearchText: Of course, it depends on her knowledge as well, but it is possible to use large mabeasts to cause major damage. It is possible, and in fact, I imagine that's the sort of thing she has actually done in the past. She could do enough to devastate a large city. That said, if you ask whether she could actually do that in the Royal Capital, Reinhard is there, so she would be stopped beforehand. There are other strong people in the Royal Capital too, such as Marcos-san, so if you're asking whether Meili alone could carry out something resembling an act of terrorism on a scale large enough to cause catastrophic damage to the Royal Capital, I don't think she could go quite that far. Meili has a pretty messed-up past, so if you wanted to get her thinking up bad things to do, she could come up with all sorts of them. So it's a good thing that she's been separated from Capella for now. If Capella and Meili had remained together all the way into Arc 10, that would have been pretty dangerous, wouldn't it? It's like, “What the hell would Capella make her do...?” (laughs)
records.arcName: Arc 10: The Land of the Lion Kings

records.question: Hello! In the final episode of the Loss Arc, the direction where Emilia brings her hand toward her mouth while letting out wordless sobs after hearing Subaru introduce himself was far too precious! Did you originally have this direction in mind, or was it something the production staff came up with through their collective wisdom?
records.answerSnippet: If you read the relevant part of Arc 6 and it's written there, then I came up with it. If it isn't written there, then the anime staff came up with it. It's that simple. (laughs) I don't think I wa...
records.answerSearchText: If you read the relevant part of Arc 6 and it's written there, then I came up with it. If it isn't written there, then the anime staff came up with it. It's that simple. (laughs) I don't think I was writing it while thinking through specific staging like, “Emilia becomes overwhelmed with emotion here, then covers her mouth with her hand...” I believe I simply wrote it in an emotional way, and then, when bringing the feeling they picked up from that writing into the anime, Director Shinohara and all the other staff members involved worked out that this would be the right way to portray it. So, if you felt that scene was particularly good, then it was entirely thanks to the contributions and efforts of the anime staff—all of the anime staff.

records.question: What Re song does Cat-sensei sing the most at karaoke??? The fans are perfect at the calls, so we're also looking forward to hearing Cat-sensei sing live at a talk show!!!!
records.answerSnippet: Redo.” (laughs) It's the song I'm most accustomed to singing, but having the series adapted into an anime was one of my dreams. Which means having an anime theme song was one of those dreams too, r...
records.answerSearchText: Redo.” (laughs) It's the song I'm most accustomed to singing, but having the series adapted into an anime was one of my dreams. Which means having an anime theme song was one of those dreams too, right? Redo left a really strong impression on me, and besides, if I sang it, everyone would get excited. (laughs) (Host: The question's “The fans are perfect at the calls, so we're also looking forward to hearing Cat-sensei sing live at a talk show!!!!” is conveyed to him.) Then please make sure you actually arrange an opportunity for that! If I did it here, it would be too noisy and people would end up saying, “What on earth is Animate doing?” But when that opportunity comes, please give me a proper call-and-response! (laughs)

records.question: Now that Schult-chan has become the lord of the Barielle domain under the name Schult Barielle, I'd like to know whether he'll grow up without training his body as Lady Priscilla instructed, or whether he'll grow up all muscular by following the methods Heinkel taught him.
records.answerSnippet: He might not become all muscular, but I do feel that he needs to have a certain degree of strength. Schult-chan should have a very strong sense that he needs to become a person worthy of being the ...
records.answerSearchText: He might not become all muscular, but I do feel that he needs to have a certain degree of strength. Schult-chan should have a very strong sense that he needs to become a person worthy of being the lord of the Barielle domain, so he should steadily grow into a solid, dependable man who won't bring shame to the name “Schult Barielle.” Right now, I think Garfiel and Schult are about the only two who are properly following the path toward becoming truly good men, so he should continue to grow properly. Though, I don't think he'll become all muscular.
records.arcName: Arc 9: Light of the Nameless Star

records.question: Cat-sensei, please tell us about some of your favorite Re episodes that even you find yourself rereading over and over! Also, since the serialization has gone on for so long, we'd love to know roughly how many times you've reread the story so far!
records.answerSnippet: I often reread things while also looking at the reactions, thinking, “I wonder what everyone thought about this.” So I tend to reread episodes that received a lot of reactions. If we're talking abo...
records.answerSearchText: I often reread things while also looking at the reactions, thinking, “I wonder what everyone thought about this.” So I tend to reread episodes that received a lot of reactions. If we're talking about how well a volume comes together as a whole, there's Volume 31, The Sword Demon Island of Ginnunhive, where Subaru spends an entire volume having a pretty miserable time. I like that volume because it comes together nicely as a single book while also having some really exciting developments, so I reread it often. Of course, I also frequently reread the volumes containing episodes I particularly like, such as Volume 6's “From Zero” and Volume 15's “Choose Me.” And I reread them to remind myself of setting details that I mustn't forget, too. Reinhard in particular is often a case of, “Wait, how much of this have I written already?” If I end up not writing something that I was supposed to write, that wouldn't be good, so I look back over things to make sure. While I'm in the middle of writing a story, I also reread episodes related to the characters who are going to appear. For example, Arc 10 is about Crusch-san, Ferris, and the others appearing again after a long absence, so I reread Arc 5 and EX1.

records.question: In Season 4, we got to see everyone's various reactions when Subaru lost his memories, but conversely, I'm curious about everyone's reactions when Subaru's name is eaten... What would that be like...?
records.answerSnippet: Since they've forgotten Subaru, they have no choice but to react to him as “someone they don't know.” As for what Subaru would do in response, there is a girl who has forgotten Subaru at the end of...
records.answerSearchText: Since they've forgotten Subaru, they have no choice but to react to him as “someone they don't know.” As for what Subaru would do in response, there is a girl who has forgotten Subaru at the end of Arc 6, so I think you'll be able to get a pretty good idea from what happens there. I won't say much more. (laughs)

records.question: I have a question about Leilani Alnair, who appeared in SCORPION TALE. The position of Sin Archbishop was passed from mother to child, but, for example, if Sirius-san and Petelgeuse had a child, would a brand-new Sin Archbishop have been born?
records.answerSnippet: There’s definitely a possibility of that happening (laughs). Of course, that would depend on whether the child born had the potential and mentality befitting a Sin Archbishop. Unfortunately, the ba...
records.answerSearchText: There’s definitely a possibility of that happening (laughs). Of course, that would depend on whether the child born had the potential and mentality befitting a Sin Archbishop. Unfortunately, the basic setting is that all the Sin Archbishops are hopeless from the moment they’re born, so... But I think the fact that Leilani-san was carrying Louis and the others in her womb for three whole years is part of the problem. Since they spent such a long time in the womb, I think they were probably heavily influenced by their mother. I'm saying this about a character I wrote myself, but Leilani-san is a pretty unpleasant person. She's the kind of awful person who stays pregnant for about three years because she thinks, “People are considerate toward pregnant women, so I'll just stay pregnant forever.” As for Petelgeuse and Sirius... as you know, Petelgeuse-san became the way he is for a particular reason, but if a child were born from Sirius, I think they'd probably turn out to be a bad kid.

records.question: I’m a big fan of Otto Suwen. I understand that Julius likes sweet things, while Otto likes spicy and bitter things, and I’d love to hear if there was an initial episode or story that led to those preferences. Since Otto was a traveling merchant, I wonder if there were times when he struggled to find enough food to eat...
records.answerSnippet: As for Otto, I think the reason is simply that “he’s a drinker.” He tends to go for strongly flavored, salty, or spicy foods as snacks to accompany alcohol. I don't think there was any particular e...
records.answerSearchText: As for Otto, I think the reason is simply that “he’s a drinker.” He tends to go for strongly flavored, salty, or spicy foods as snacks to accompany alcohol. I don't think there was any particular episode where he explicitly “discovered” his love for spicy food. Julius isn't particularly good with alcohol, but I have the image of him as someone who knows how to properly appreciate it—enjoying the taste and aroma of wine. Otto, on the other hand, is the type to just knock it back, isn't he? (laughs) So they're contrasted there as well. (Back when Otto was poor,) there were probably times when he drank lots of cheap liquor that was easy to get, and I think there were probably also times when he was so short on food that he chewed on grass roots. He must have eaten them while saying something like, “This isn't really something I'm supposed to eat, but...”

records.question: I believe Frederica-sama was imprisoned in Wrath IF. What was Clind-san doing at that time?
records.answerSnippet: He probably got taken out by Cecilus and Halibel... When Roswaal is gone, Clind can't fight at full strength, but he still goes to rescue Frederica, so as a result... That's probably what happened....
records.answerSearchText: He probably got taken out by Cecilus and Halibel... When Roswaal is gone, Clind can't fight at full strength, but he still goes to rescue Frederica, so as a result... That's probably what happened. Frederica doesn't know about Clind-san's death.

records.question: There are sometimes characters who can use powers resembling Authorities despite not possessing a Witch Factor. Apparently, one of the conditions required to “open the door” is having a “profound connection.” What kind of conditions fulfill that requirement?
records.answerSnippet: First of all, in the world of Re:Zero, there is a powerful force called an Authority, which is used by the Sin Archbishops. And there are also people who have a deep connection with the Witch Cult ...
records.answerSearchText: First of all, in the world of Re:Zero, there is a powerful force called an Authority, which is used by the Sin Archbishops. And there are also people who have a deep connection with the Witch Cult or the Sin Archbishops who are able to use powers resembling Authorities. Among them are characters who possess special abilities that have nothing to do with Authorities at all, including abilities that were being developed to counter Authorities other than Divine Protections, as well as various individuals with supernatural abilities who can use things resembling teleportation. There was that expression, “opening the door,” but the idea is that they're bringing in powers that don't originally exist on this side. In short, being around someone who possesses incredible power causes you to be influenced by them, making it easier for you to open that door. Something as simple as spending a long time together, being blood relatives, or having a contractual relationship like Subaru and Beatrice, for example. I think there can probably also be cases where the door opens through a chain reaction. Things like distance, the depth of the relationship, and blood ties can play a role as well... Though it ultimately becomes a matter of intuition.

records.question: Subaru's birthday is April 1st, but have you decided what year he was born?
records.answerSnippet: Let's not decide that. If we establish a birth year, explaining why he had a flip phone becomes complicated, and then when people look at the series in the future, they might start thinking about h...
records.answerSearchText: Let's not decide that. If we establish a birth year, explaining why he had a flip phone becomes complicated, and then when people look at the series in the future, they might start thinking about his actual age and go, “Wait, so he's supposed to be...?” and things like that. Let's just leave the birth year undecided (laughs). Sorry!

records.question: I have a question about the scene in Arc 9 where Al brings out the Book of the Dead. When Petra read Subaru's Book of the Dead, it only contained memories up to the Sanctuary, but when Al shared the information with the Divine Dragon, I believe the memories that were shared went all the way to the end. Why was that?
records.answerSnippet: Subaru's Book of the Dead is one of multiple books, each of which records his memories up until the time he died, whereas Al only has one book. Since Al has only one book, he had an incredibly diff...
records.answerSearchText: Subaru's Book of the Dead is one of multiple books, each of which records his memories up until the time he died, whereas Al only has one book. Since Al has only one book, he had an incredibly difficult time searching for it. He had to redo things over and over again before finally finding it, and then he used the book he had found in that way. As for the episode where Al hid Subaru's Book of the Dead, it was a time-delayed trap: “If Petra and Meili find out that there's a book hidden by Al, then naturally they'll search for it and read it.” Of course, even Al doesn't know which of Subaru's deaths the particular book records. The fact that the book I happened to leave there was specifically the one from the loop where Petra gave Subaru the handkerchief was simply my own malicious intent (laughs). That's basically how it happened.
records.arcName: Arc 9: Light of the Nameless Star

records.question: I have a question about the Great Spirit OdGlass. I believe it was mentioned that its appearance resembles a polar bear, but what kind of abilities does it specifically have? If it isn't a spoiler, I'd love to know.
records.answerSnippet: OdGlass is the one that makes the snow fall in the northern Holy Kingdom of Gusteko, and OdGlass knows everything that is happening within the area where the snow is falling. There is a religion in...
records.answerSearchText: OdGlass is the one that makes the snow fall in the northern Holy Kingdom of Gusteko, and OdGlass knows everything that is happening within the area where the snow is falling. There is a religion in Gusteko called the Gusteko Holy Church that worships spirits, and the head of that religion is the Holy King, who is also the nation's head of state. The Holy King enters into a contract with OdGlass. As a result, the Holy King demonstrates his authority by being able to know everything about Gusteko and deal with every bad thing that happens there. That's why the ultimate goal of the Gusteko Holy Church is to cover the entire world in snow. If they do that, they'll be able to know everything that happens in that world. So, I'd like you to read Re:Zero while thinking, “Huh, so there are people in the north who are aiming for something like that...” (laughs).

records.question: I really love Cecilus-kun and Arakiya-chan, so I was really shocked by the story in Sasageru IF where the two of them had a child. I'd love to hear about the circumstances and episodes that led up to that, if there are any.
records.answerSnippet: When I was writing Sasageru, those two just went ahead and got married on their own, so I don't really know either (laughs). It was only when I decided I wanted to write about 400 years in the futu...
records.answerSearchText: When I was writing Sasageru, those two just went ahead and got married on their own, so I don't really know either (laughs). It was only when I decided I wanted to write about 400 years in the future that I started thinking about it for the first time. When I thought about what kind of people would still be around 400 years later... there'd be Arakiya, whose lifespan had effectively become endless because she'd practically merged with a spirit, and Madelyn, who's a dragon-human, and so on. I was also able to bring in the grown-up versions of the quasi-spirits accompanying Julius, something I'd originally thought would be nice to do somewhere someday. When I started thinking, “What is Arakiya's motivation for still being around in the present day (400 years later)?” protecting Vollachia would naturally be one of them, especially because of her connection with Priscilla. But if Cecilus were to disappear, Arakiya's mental balance would probably become seriously unstable. So maybe Cecilus is taking responsibility before he dies. But unfortunately, Cecilus's way of taking responsibility would be the Vollachian way, and Rowan-san wasn't exactly a good father—so, after considering all those things, I think I had Arakiya have descendants so that she wouldn't lose her reason for living. I imagine the proposal itself was probably very casual. Cecilus is the type who acts once he's made up his mind, so he might have said something like, “Anya always challenges me, but I think it's about time I got a prize if I beat you.” Arakiya would then challenge him by saying, “You won't beat me, so sure,” giving him her word. After their usual playful back-and-forth, Cecilus wins and says, “Then let's get married,” and that's probably how they got married. And then Arakiya, having already said what she said, would be like, “Gnnnnngh...” — followed by marriage, followed by a child, followed by their descendants eventually going extinct... I think that's probably how it went. The details of the individual episodes might be a little rough, but I think that's roughly the idea as it stands now!

records.question: A question about Anime Season 4. I believe Anastasia was split in half several times, but which Anastasia is your favorite?
records.answerSnippet: I guess Episode 3 (Episode 69 overall), right? (laughs) The one where she goes BAM! right in front of Subaru. Honestly, I was wondering how they were going to do that—whether they'd use all sorts o...
records.answerSearchText: I guess Episode 3 (Episode 69 overall), right? (laughs) The one where she goes BAM! right in front of Subaru. Honestly, I was wondering how they were going to do that—whether they'd use all sorts of techniques to make sure you couldn't see too much—but then I thought, “Ah, I see. So this is how they can get away with showing it these days.” I also like the part where Subaru comes up the spiral staircase absolutely brimming with murderous intent, and Anastasia is hanging upside down on the stairs. She has this sort of utterly indifferent look on her face... I'm starting to sound like a really messed-up person, aren't I? (laughs)

records.question: Is there a Book of the Dead for Ryuzu Meyer in the Great Library Pleiades?
records.answerSnippet: There is. Reading it would probably be pretty heartbreaking... At the end, the episode that everyone knows about is what comes out. I'm glad that people care about Ryuzu-san. Recently, Comic Alive ...
records.answerSearchText: There is. Reading it would probably be pretty heartbreaking... At the end, the episode that everyone knows about is what comes out. I'm glad that people care about Ryuzu-san. Recently, Comic Alive published a little episode featuring young Beatrice and Ryuzu, along with Roswaal and Echidna from the teacher's side, drawn by Ms. Atori and Ms. Aikawa, who are working on the Chapter 4 manga adaptation. If you're interested, please check it out! (*) I think it'll probably be included in a collected volume, so please look forward to it. They came to me with the proposal, saying, “We'd like to do this episode,” and I read it and thought, “That's a really great story!” So I gave them the OK.

records.question: In Arc 9, it was said that anyone can use the Witch Factor of Melancholy as long as they pay the price. Is the Witch Factor of Vainglory similar in that regard?
records.answerSnippet: he Witch Factor of Melancholy is in a state where, so to speak, its ownership is unassigned, because Hector-san, who originally possessed it, is no longer around. (That's why anyone can use it.) Va...
records.answerSearchText: he Witch Factor of Melancholy is in a state where, so to speak, its ownership is unassigned, because Hector-san, who originally possessed it, is no longer around. (That's why anyone can use it.) Vainglory is similar in terms of its underlying setting, but it was specifically made to suit Pandora-san, and Pandora hasn't let go of it, so under the current circumstances, it would be difficult. However, if Pandora-san were to die and the ownership were to become unassigned, it should be possible to use it under the same conditions.
records.arcName: Arc 9: Light of the Nameless Star

records.question: his is about SCORPION TALE. Apparently, there was an organisation called the Saintess Sect 400 years ago. Could you give us a little information about it?
records.answerSnippet: The leader of the Saintess Sect was someone named Pandora-san (laughs). As you can probably tell by now, it was basically the Witch Cult. The Saintess Sect was the predecessor to the Witch Cult. Ju...
records.answerSearchText: The leader of the Saintess Sect was someone named Pandora-san (laughs). As you can probably tell by now, it was basically the Witch Cult. The Saintess Sect was the predecessor to the Witch Cult. Juice and the others created the Witch Cult in order to help witches who were being persecuted. At the time, the Witch Cult was engaged in genuinely good activities, somewhat like the way things were when Emilia and Fortuna-san were in the Elior Forest. However, the Witch Cult was eventually absorbed into the Saintess Sect, and the name “Saintess Sect” wasn't spreading in a particularly positive way, so the organization eventually went through a transition where they decided, “Then let's borrow the name of the Witch Cult that we absorbed.” Basically, you can think of the Saintess Sect as having been doing the kinds of things that the Witch Cult does today. I think that's an accurate way of understanding it.
